title: Tally: Non-Intrusive Performance Isolation for Concurrent Deep Learning Workloads
problem: GPU sharing for concurrent deep learning workloads suffers from high interference between co-running jobs, causing up to 188.9% latency overhead on high-priority inference tasks. Existing GPU sharing mechanisms impose high integration costs, offer inadequate performance isolation, and have limited application compatibility.
motivation: GPU underutilization in production DL clusters leads to prolonged job queues and increased operational costs, making efficient multi-tenant GPU sharing a critical challenge.
method: Tally implements a non-intrusive GPU sharing mechanism based on fine-grained thread-block-level kernel scheduling. It intercepts GPU kernel launches and dynamically schedules thread blocks across co-running workloads without requiring application modification, allowing the system to control interference between high-priority inference and best-effort training tasks at the thread-block granularity rather than at the kernel or process level.
key_novelty: Thread-block-level GPU kernel scheduling that enforces performance isolation between concurrent workloads without any application-side code changes or framework integration.
contributions: Non-intrusive GPU sharing mechanism requiring no modification to user applications or frameworks
Fine-grained thread-block-level scheduling strategy that effectively mitigates co-execution interference
Evaluation showing only 7.2% P99 latency overhead on inference tasks vs. 188.9% for state-of-the-art TGS
Demonstration of >80% throughput retention relative to TGS while providing robust isolation

metrics.other: P99 latency overhead: 7.2% (Tally) vs. 188.9% (TGS); throughput: >80% of TGS

limitations: Not discussed; throughput is >80% of TGS but still below exclusive execution baselines.
primary_theme: GPU multi-tenant scheduling with performance isolation
